input:
Tuesday works. Also, can we talk about how reporting integrates with our existing policyholder records?
The customer is unsure how reporting will integrate with their existing policyholder records.

We’re seeing a duplicate loss report scenario where the same incident comes in via phone and portal, creating two claims without any intake warning — we’ve even spotted disabled UI buttons that should allow linking but don’t work.
Duplicate loss reports create multiple claims without any warning or ability to link them.

Finance is questioning which figure is correct because the export doesn’t match the dashboard — the export figures mismatch is causing delays in our month-end close.
Finance cannot determine the correct figure because exported data does not match the dashboard.

I’m trying to set up some saved filters on the claims list to help my team track high-priority cases, but I can’t seem to lock them in properly.
The user cannot lock saved filters on the claims list.

First, we need to set up a custom claim-reference format — our internal systems rely on specific prefixes and sequences... we can’t have mismatches when pulling reports or syncing with suppliers.
The platform does not allow us to define a custom claim‑reference format that matches our internal naming conventions.

Yes, we’re in the middle of preparing for renewal and have a specific ask around correspondence formats.
The customer cannot easily adjust correspondence formats needed for claims reporting during renewal.

we’re still evaluating how Keelwater fits our claims workflow, especially around reserves and supplier payments...
They are uncertain how Keelwater integrates with their claims workflow, particularly for reserves and supplier payments.

The interface changes last month moved key controls without warning — we had to retrain staff because of those unexpected interface changes.
Unexpected interface changes forced staff to be retrained.

Our motor teams are pushing for automated claim routing by postcode and workload, but our commercial teams need manual claim routing for complex cases — we really need configuration that varies by team to keep everyone happy.
Motor and commercial teams clash over claim routing because one wants automation by postcode and workload while the other requires manual handling for complex cases.

We’re getting pressure ... they need official correspondence in their own language. Specifically, ... Welsh letter formats for claims and payments.
The company lacks Welsh-language letter formats for claims and payments, causing pressure from Welsh policyholders.

Hi Bryn, I’m Quenna from Penhallow Specialty Risks — we’re having trouble accessing our reserves dashboard after the update last week.
The customer cannot access the reserves dashboard after a recent update.

Hi Carys, we’re setting up our team workflows and need clarity on how claim allocation works across different lines.
Unclear how claim allocation works across different lines when setting up team workflows.

We’ve got three claims stuck waiting on garage replies again today.
Claims are delayed because they are waiting for garage responses.

I’m trying to get a batch of claim docs into the system for Kilnsey Household but it’s taking ages one by one. Any way to speed this up?
Uploading claim documents one by one is painfully slow.

Perfect, and if you can flag any pending letters or documents that might be blocked too, that’d help us plan ahead.
They cannot see in advance which pending letters or documents might be blocked, making planning difficult.

Second, we’re getting the same claim twice when a policyholder reports via phone and then the portal — no alert pops up at intake.
Duplicate claims are created when a policyholder reports the same incident by phone and then through the portal, and no alert is generated.

We’re getting repeated feedback on renewal price concern — especially from our high-ARR clients — and it’s becoming a blocker for retention unless we get clarity soon.
Customers are worried about renewal pricing, which is threatening retention.

Exactly — and it’s not just annoying, it’s eating into time we could spend on policyholders or tasks.
The current process is annoying and consumes time that could be used for policyholders or other tasks.

We’re also struggling with task assignments and letter generation—sometimes policyholders don’t get timely updates.
The team has difficulty assigning tasks and generating letters, leading to delayed updates for policyholders.

We’re still having to call garages ourselves every day because the repair updates missing from the system — it’s becoming a real time-sink for our handlers.
Handlers must manually call garages daily because repair updates are missing from the system, wasting time.

we’re running claims reports late into the evening and the bright interface is straining our eyes...Any chance we can get dark mode enabled?
The user finds the bright interface hard on their eyes during late‑night claim report work.

That would be great — I’m under the impression I’m assigned the right role, but maybe something’s misconfigured on our end.
The user suspects their role is misconfigured, preventing proper access.

We’re having trouble pulling the latest reserves report for our policyholders — it’s showing outdated figures even after we refreshed the tasks list.
The reserves report shows outdated figures even after refreshing the task list.

When a reserve exceeds authority and the approver’s out with no delegate, it just piles… it’s claims stalling until someone returns.
Approvals get stuck when a reserve exceeds authority and no delegate is assigned, causing delays.

Appreciate that. Also, any update on when policyholders will start getting those milestone updates automatically?
Policyholders are not receiving milestone updates automatically.

We’ve got claims stuck because the reserve change needs approval, and with the approver away and no delegate, the approval waiting list just grows — it’s not sustainable.
Claims get stuck because reserve changes require approval, and there’s no delegate when the approver is away.

That’s exactly what I’m after — especially how roles affect who can adjust those reserves before payment triggers.
Unclear how role permissions impact adjusting reserves before payment triggers.

Right now it’s a mix of spreadsheets and email threads — not ideal when we need to assign tasks or generate letters for policyholders.
The team relies on spreadsheets and email threads to manage tasks and create policyholder letters, which is inefficient.

I need to reset my password for the claims portal — can you help me with that right away?
The user cannot access the claims portal because they forgot their password.

That’d be great — we’ve got policyholders waiting on letters, and tasks are piling up because the reporting module’s stuck.
The reporting module is stuck, causing delays in sending letters to policyholders and a backlog of tasks.

Great. We’re swamped with letters and payments too — anything to reduce that load helps.
The team is overwhelmed by the volume of letters and payment processing.

And the unexpected interface changes — last week the Claims Tasks panel vanished without warning, and we had to retrain our team mid-week.
Unexpected interface changes disrupt workflow and require unplanned retraining.

The issue is that reserve updates beyond handler limits are stuck waiting for sign-off with no backup approver, causing a reserve authorisation delay that halts payments and reporting.
Reserve updates that exceed a handler's limit get stuck waiting for sign‑off because there is no backup approver, causing delays that stop payments and reporting.

One last thing — can we trial the roles and tasks features before committing?
The customer is unsure about committing to the roles and tasks features without trying them first.

Appreciate the quick response — just let me know if you need any login details or supplier IDs to troubleshoot.
The customer needs to provide login details or supplier IDs for troubleshooting.

we’re manually sending claim progress messages, but it’s time-consuming and inconsistent... manually drafting and sending claim progress messages to keep policyholders informed, but it’s inefficient and error-prone.
Manually drafting and sending claim progress messages is time‑consuming, inconsistent, and error‑prone.

Administration: click "Overview", dead x1
The admin cannot access the Overview page because it results in a dead end.
